This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Windsor Johnston. A major nor'easter is making its way
up the coast, disrupting Thanksgiving travel plans and holiday events. In New York City,
the Macy's Thanksgiving Day parade has been moved to Saturday, the first time it's been postponed
in its 100-year history. Mayor Zoran Mamdani says the city made the decision to protect people,
taking part in the parade and the crowds along the route.
This decision, as you heard, was made in coordination with Macy's, the NYPD,
and many agency partners. Safety is and will always remain our top priority,
and this will be a heavy storm. We are expecting sustained winds between 30 and 40 miles per hour,
with gusts as high as 60 to 65 miles per hour possible.
On the West Coast, unusually high tides are prompting coastal flood warnings.
In Northern California, evacuation orders and warnings have been issued for several communities.
U.S. intelligence officials have told congressional staff there's no evidence
that China's spy services orchestrated the affair between NVIDIA chief Jensen Huang
and a Chinese tech executive. NPR's Ryan Lucas has more.
American intelligence officials told Congress there is no evidence so far that Alice Huang
began her affair with Jensen Huang at the direction of Chinese intelligence,
but she is believed to have passed along information once the romantic relationship began.
That's according to a person familiar with the matter who was granted anonymity to discuss a
closed-door briefing. The officials also said the information so far does not indicate that Alice
Huang is a spy or an asset of China's intelligence services. There is more evidence, though,
that her associate, Kang Wei, has such ties. While Jensen Huang's affair has generated headlines,
experts say the bigger national security threat is the diversion of NVIDIA's most
advanced AI chips to China. Ryan Lucas, NPR News, Washington.
The Federal Communications Commission has authorized SpaceX to build and launch up to
one million satellites for its planned orbital data centers. NPR's Jeff Brumfield has more.
In its authorization, the FCC said SpaceX could place the satellites in six different
orbital shells around the Earth. With its solar panels and radiators deployed,
each satellite is roughly 10 stories tall and as wide as a Boeing 747 jumbo jet.
SpaceX wants to build the millionth satellite constellation as part of an AI computing project
it calls StarMind. Elon Musk says AI data centers in space will be cheaper to operate because power
is free. Critics warn the technology is unproven and could lead to a huge increase in space debris.
Jeff Brumfield, NPR News. At the close on Wall Street,
the Dow was up 164 points. This is NPR News. The Pittsburgh Steelers have released veteran
quarterback and four-time MVP Aaron Rodgers. The decision came after the team bench Rodgers last
night over his criticism of the coach. Jeremy Scott from member station WESA reports.
Less than a day after the Steelers announced they were benching Rodgers,
the Super Bowl champion quarterback criticized Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy on ESPN's
The Pat McAfee Show, saying McCarthy fell asleep last week in a team meeting and identified the
Steelers as the Green Bay Packers during a recent team huddle when the Steelers were visiting the
Philadelphia Eagles. McCarthy did not offer many specifics on the release of Rodgers but said about
his benching. It was a process that you know went on throughout this week and we got to a point
we talked about some communication and things like that and there was an ultimatum made clearly out
of the side of his job description so it was my decision to bench him. The team is named Mason
Rudolph, the starting quarterback moving forward. For NPR News, I'm Jeremy Scott in Pittsburgh.
Major League Baseball is asking a federal judge in New York City to rule that a lockout team owners
are considering for next week would be legal under federal antitrust law. The league and all 30 teams
sued the Players Union and eight members of its executive subcommittee. The owners are trying to
head off a possible antitrust challenge if players decertify the union. Stocks traded mixed on Wall
Street today, the Dow up 164 points, NASDAQ down 147. This is NPR. Want to hear this podcast without

topics.text: Nor'easter disrupts Thanksgiving travel, and NYC moves Macy's Thanksgiving Day parade to Saturday
Unusually high tides prompt coastal flood warnings on the West Coast, with evacuation orders in Northern California
U.S. intelligence finds no evidence China's spy services orchestrated Jensen Huang's affair with Alice Huang
FCC authorizes SpaceX to build and launch up to one million satellites for orbital data centers
Pittsburgh Steelers release quarterback Aaron Rodgers after he criticized head coach Mike McCarthy
MLB asks federal judge in New York to rule that a planned owners' lockout is legal
Wall Street closes mixed, with the Dow up 164 points and the NASDAQ down 147
